subject: Dedicated reservation: flexible floor + burst lanes for Hydrolytics
messages:
From: Taylor Reed <taylor@hydrolytics.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity ask + preferred commitment shapes

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo — the latency profile and autoscale behavior looked promising. We're finalizing a recommended infra shape and procurement timeline and would like a written proposal that specifically lays out:

- Minimum guaranteed GPU floor options (per region) we can sign up for (monthly commitments).
- Staged ramp schedules (how we can start small and reach peak over 3–6 months).
- Burst lanes / emergency capacity behavior (how much we can exceed floor, for how long, at what price).
- The short list of GPU SKUs you support for our model family (we run a mix of 35B and 70B LLMs).

Attaching our demand profile so you can map traffic spikes. Our procurement team is asking for 3 scenarios: conservative, target, and high. Procurement lead is looped (procure@hydrolytics.ai) — they prefer a price anchor by GPU-hour and by sustained token throughput if possible.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week to walk through.

Thanks,
Taylor

--
Taylor Reed
Head of ML Engineering, Hydrolytics
T: +1 415-555-0123

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask + preferred commitment shapes

Hi Taylor — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. I've pasted an initial, high-level approach below and attached two spreadsheets: a quick ramp worksheet and a draft SOW.

High-level options (very terse):
1) Soft-floor (flexible reserve) — small monthly commit (e.g., 4 GPUs sustained) + auto-burst pool. Lower upfront; higher per-burst rate. Good if you want limited commitment to start.
2) Graduated commit (stair-step) — commit at 8 GPUs month 1, 16 GPUs month 3, 32 GPUs month 6. We give stepped discounts at each activation.
3) Anchor + buffer (recommended for production) — anchor minimal persistent pool (12 GPUs) for predictable latency + a 20% guaranteed burst capacity for sudden load. Includes 24/7 prefail routing and cross-region fallback.

Technical assumptions used for numbers: average sequence lengths, 35B and 70B model latency per-token, typical caching hit-rates. Jonas (cc'd) will add the SKU-level guidance.

Request: can you confirm whether your 3 scenarios should be framed as sustained average throughput (tokens/sec) or as peak concurrent sessions? Procurement typically asks for both but we'll surface one canonical anchor.

Call options: Wed 9/2 10:00am PT or Thu 9/3 2:00pm PT.

Attachments: Redwood_Interim_Ramp_Scenarios.xlsx; Draft_SOW_Redwood.pdf

Best,
Olga

Hey Taylor — quick tech note to help map commitment tiers to expected throughput: 

- Supported SKUs we recommend: H100-80GB for 70B models (best latency), A100-40GB for 35B with mixed precision. We can provide quantized 4-bit runs for cost reduction (with customer QA).
- Baseline throughput estimates (single model instance): H100 ~ 18–22 tokens/sec for 70B at batch=1; A100 ~ 9–12 tokens/sec for 35B. These are conservative for safety.
- Minimum practical sustained lane: 4 GPUs for low-latency production (ensures KV cache warm / hot-path). Anything below that risks cold-start p99 spikes.
- Burst lanes: we can pre-allocate a burst pool that sits idle until invoked; typical policy: charged at a premium (1.6–2.0x) and auto-deallocates after a 30-minute inactivity window.

I'll populate the attached Ramp_Scenarios with per-GPU throughput lines so Olga can convert to pricing rows.

-Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Taylor Reed <taylor@hydrolytics.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@hydrolytics.ai
Date: 2026-09-03T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask + preferred commitment shapes

Thanks — that helps. Procurement's asks below. Sorry for the long list, but they want it in one doc for legal review: 

- Explicit minimal guaranteed GPU floor (monthly) with cancellation windows and notice periods.
- Overage pricing for burst usage and details on burst caps (per-day and per-month).
- Credits or service-level credits if we get sustained p99 violations beyond the floor.
- Transferability between regions (we occasionally shift capacity between us-west and us-east).
- A clear activation cadence: when we say "start month 1" what is the earliest activation date and lead time to provision additional GPUs?

Procurement also wanted to see two pricing shapes: a high-commit discount (12+ month term) and a short-term onramp (3-month term) so they can compare TCO.

Can you add these to the SOW and send a consolidated PDF? We're aiming to complete vendor selection by 9/15.

Taylor

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Taylor Reed <taylor@hydrolytics.ai>, procure@hydrolytics.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-07T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity ask + preferred commitment shapes

Taylor / Procurement team — attached is a consolidated proposal PDF and a short one-page pricing summary. Key callouts below (concise):

Option A — Soft-floor (Low commitment)
- Guarantee: 4 GPUs sustained (monthly), on-demand burst up to +50% of baseline for short windows.
- Ramp: immediate activation (48–72 hour lead for baseline); burst available on first day.
- Pricing: standard hosted hourly + burst multiplier 1.8x.
- Term: month-to-month.

Option B — Graduated commit (Onramp plan) — recommended if you want predictable cost while growing
- Guarantee: 8 GPUs month 1, 16 GPUs month 3, 32 GPUs month 6 (we implement activation triggers at 30% utilization thresholds).
- Ramp: each step has 7–14 day provisioning lead time (we reserve capacity ahead of activation windows).
- Pricing: stepped discount: 5% @8, 12% @16, 20% @32 across committed GPU hours.
- Term: 6 months with optional extension.

Option C — Anchor + Buffer (Production SLA) — recommended for mission-critical products
- Guarantee: 12 GPUs persistent + guaranteed 20% burst buffer (immediately available). Cross-region fallback to east region within 2 hours.
- Ramp: activation of additional 8 GPUs within 24–48 hours when invoked.
- Pricing: greater upfront commit discount; includes 1 SLA credit entitlement tier if p99 latency breaches exceed agreed SLOs.
- Term: 12 month minimum.

Other notes:
- Cancellation & notices: 30-day notice for soft-floor; 60-day for graduated; 90-day for anchor contracts (standardized).
- Burst caps: default daily cap of 2x baseline for safety; can be raised to 3x with advance notice and financial holdback.
- Transferability: we support intra-account region transfer where capacity is available; cross-region transfer fees may apply to reserved hours.
- Lead times: 48–72 hours for soft baseline; up to 14 days for large step activations if we need to mobilize additional racks.

Attachments: Draft_SOW_Redwood.pdf; Pricing_Tiers_v2.xlsx; Hydrolytics_Demand_Profile.xlsx

Next steps:
1) We will update the SOW to include your requested legal clauses and the two term-based pricing shapes (3-month, 12-month) by 9/10.
2) Ben will follow up with a line-item pricing sheet.
3) If procurement wants a live walkthrough of the ramp table, Jonas can share a small simulation.

Can we lock in a follow-up 30-min call on 9/10 11:00am PT?

Thanks — Olga
